meta.title: Findings: single questions read directly
meta.question: What do decision-makers say vendors focus on, what does it cost, and how low is the bar?
meta.unit: share of all respondents (n = 319) per answer; or number of written answers
caveats: Each chart reads one question as asked; no result is subtracted from another question's result.
Shares are of all 319 respondents (group-level); one-answer questions add to 100%, pick-several questions do not.
Quotes are verbatim; which quotes to show was chosen by Claude (06_visualization/quote_picks.csv).
Behaviour counts are written answers coded by one coder, checked blind on 200 answers (behaviour alpha 0.87).
meta.provenance: Question wording VERBATIM; shares RECON_DATA; quote selection and behaviour codes INFERRED.

q14.stem: Thinking of a typical meeting with a vendor sales team (or person), how would you characterize their agenda in your interactions? Please pick the one that best matches your opinion of the majority of sales calls you participate in.

items.label: Thinking of a typical meeting with a vendor sales team (or person), how would you characterize their agenda in your interactions? Please pick the one that best matches your opinion of the majority of sales calls you participate in.

options.label: They only want to tell me about their products and services and present what they do.
They listen for a key word or two so they can launch into a prepared pitch about how they relate to that topic.
They are legitimately interested in trying to help us understand how their products or services would work...
They try to understand our challenges and offer suggestions (even if they don't sell those products and services)...
They are genuinely interested in partnering with us to make sure our initiative is successful.

q8.stem: When you meet with a vendor sales person, in general how often are they prepared for the meeting with you in the following ways?

items.label: Knowledgeable about their company and products
Knowledgeable about my industry
Knowledgeable about my specific business
Can relate to my role and responsibilities in the organization
Understands my issues and where they can help

q18.stem: Considering the materials that vendors typically provide you with, which of the following best describe how well those materials helps you develop convincing reasons to invest?

items.label: Considering the materials that vendors typically provide you with, which of the following best describe how well those materials helps you develop convincing reasons to invest?

options.label: It would be a simple task for me to develop convincing business justification for the purchase.
I can quantify specific impacts and how they change for different environments. Limited customization necessary.
I can quantify specific impacts, but not how they change for different environments. Significant customization necessary
I can identify potential impact, but not quantify them. We had to do most of the business justification ourselves.
Limited materials were provided. We had to do all of the business justification ourselves.

behaviours.label: Puts my needs before their sale

quotes.why: worst teams: selling product instead of solving the business problem
quotes.text: too many to mention but they all have same qualities - hard sell their products rather than helping me solve business problems

quotes.why: worst relationships: more interested in selling than solving business challenges
quotes.text: sales reps for certain companies - more interested in selling than solving my business challenges.

quotes.why: worst relationships: closing the sale; not understanding the problem
quotes.text: Sales Man/Rep - focused totally on closing a sale.  Don't understand the issues/problems I'm trying to solve.

quotes.why: worst teams: not focused on my needs
quotes.text: Not focused on my needs.  Intersted more in a sale.

quotes.why: worst relationships: no idea how they fit our company
quotes.text: acct mgr becuase they dont understand how they fit into our company only what they want to sell

quotes.why: worst teams: knowledgeable but focused on selling more
quotes.text: IBM - knowledgeable but mainly focused on selling more equipment

quotes.why: best teams: did their homework on our company
quotes.text: They have done their homework on our company, they listen carefully to understand our business problems and suggest best approaches to solving those problems.

quotes.why: best teams: know my issues before I tell them
quotes.text: Accenture, IBM, E&Y...they are current on my industry trends and know my issues before I tell them.

quotes.why: worst teams: expected us to complete their business case
quotes.text: Merlot - wanted us to work on their schedule  AdOpt - expected us to complete their business case NavTech - partial solutions
KAM: understands how my company works and helps sell internally

quotes.why: best relationships: benefit in terms of efficiency and ROI
quotes.text: product specialist, because he understands our needs and knows how his services can benefit us in terms of efficiency and ROI

quotes.why: best teams: know my needs and don't oversell
quotes.text: Xerox know my needs and don't oversell IBM know our business and always coming to see us to ensure the products match our needs

quotes.why: best relationships: span the chasm between my problems and their solutions
quotes.text: Technical Field Engineer/Sales Engineer - they understand my industry, my problems and can span the chasm between my problems and their solutions.

quotes.why: best teams: step in our shoes
quotes.text: NSI, BT, DHL, all step in our shoes
